description:
(Summary from jobright.ai; the original posting may say more.)

Apple develops innovative hardware, software, and services that create products and customer experiences used by millions of people. The Software Engineer: Linux Driver and Kernel Developer will develop Linux device drivers and user-land tests for validating subsystems in complex SoCs, implement board support packages, perform software bring-up, and debug hardware and software issues.
Linux kernel and device-driver engineer for SoC subsystems, BSP bring-up, validation, and hardware debugging

Responsibilities:
• Work closely with designers and architects to understand functional IP blocks and their use cases
• Implement BSP and perform software bring-up on pre- and post-silicon platforms
• Develop Linux device drivers and user-land tests for exercising and validating the various subsystems in complex SoCs
• Debug and root-cause a variety of hardware and software issues

Requirements:
• Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field

Preferred:
• Experience in embedded Linux kernel development
• Experience in C programming
• Experience with ARM architecture
• Familiarity with the Linux graphics stack (Mesa, Vulkan/OpenGL, GPU compute)
• Experience validating GPUs with graphics and compute workloads, stress tests, or conformance suites (e.g., Vulkan CTS, igt-gpu-tools)
• Knowledge of Linux kernel internals (process scheduler, memory management, concurrency/synchronization, memory allocation, and file systems) and networking or storage subsystem architecture
• Device driver development and support across one or more of the following: USB, networking, graphics, video, storage, and power management
• Debugging skills in kernel space
• Experience exercising and validating systems from user space, including knowledge of user space APIs
• Experience porting and/or maintaining a Linux distribution for a platform
